entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 56 Is 56:1-12 . The Preparation Needed on the Part of Those Who Wish to Be Admitted to the Kingdom of God. 1. judgment-- equity. John the Baptist preached similarly a return to righteousness, as needed to prepare men for Messiah's first coming ( Lu 3:3 , 8-14 ). So it shall be before the second coming (Mal 4:4-6). near to come-- ( Mt 3:2 ; 4:17 ), also as to the second coming ( Is 62:10 , 11 ; Lu 21:28 , 31 ; Ro 13:11 , 12 ; He 10:25 ). righteousness-- answering to "salvation" in the parallel clause; therefore it means righteousness which bringeth salvation ( Is 46:13 ; Ro 3:25 , 26 ).

(<reference osisRef="Luke.12.43">Lu 12:43</reference>).<div eID="gen16213" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16214" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the man--</hi>Hebrew, enosh, "a man in humble life," in contradistinction to Hebrew, ish, "one of high rank." Even the humblest, as "the stranger" and "the eunuch" (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.4">Is 56:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.56.6">6</reference>), are admissible to these privileges.<div eID="gen16214" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16215" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">this ... it--</hi>what follows: "keeping the Sabbath," &c. (<reference osisRef="Isa.58.13">Is 58:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.58.14">14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.12">Eze 20:12</reference>). A proof that the Sabbath, in the spirit of its obligation, was to be binding under the Gospel (<reference osisRef="Isa.66.23">Is 66:23</reference>). That gospel times are referred to is plain, from the blessing not being pronounced on the man who observed the sacrificial ritual of the Jewish law.<div eID="gen16215" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16216" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">layeth hold--</hi>image from one grasping firmly some precious object which he is afraid of having forcibly snatched from him. Together, they form the whole duty of man, the worship of God and a holy life. <div eID="gen16217" type="x-p"/>

They shall no longer be confined as proselytes were, to the outer court, but shall be admitted "into the holiest" (<reference osisRef="Heb.10.19">He 10:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Heb.10.20">20</reference>).<div eID="gen16225" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16226" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">a place--</hi>literally, "a hand."<div eID="gen16226" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16227" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">than of sons--</hi>Though the eunuch is barren of children (<reference osisRef="Isa.56.3">Is 56:3</reference>), I will give him a more lasting name than that of being father of sons and daughters (regarded as a high honor among the Hebrews) (<reference osisRef="John.1.12">Joh 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.10.3">10:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="1John.3.1">1Jo 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.17">Re 2:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.3.12">3:12</reference>). <div eID="gen16227" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 5. in mine house-- the temple, the emblem of the Church ( 1Ti 3:15 ). They shall no longer be confined as proselytes were, to the outer court, but shall be admitted "into the holiest" ( He 10:19 , 20 ). a place-- literally, "a hand." than of sons-- Though the eunuch is barren of children ( Is 56:3 ), I will give him a more lasting name than that of being father of sons and daughters (regarded as a high honor among the Hebrews) ( Joh 1:12 ; 10:3 ; 1Jo 3:1 ; Re 2:17 ; 3:12 ).

Even them--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Eph.2.11-Eph.2.13">Ep 2:11-13</reference>).<div eID="gen16229" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16230" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to my holy mountain--</hi>Jerusalem, the seat of the Lord's throne in His coming kingdom (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.2">Is 2:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.3.17">Jr 3:17</reference>).<div eID="gen16230" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16231" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">joyful--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Rom.5.11">Ro 5:11</reference>).<div eID="gen16231" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16232" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">burnt offerings ... sacrifices--</hi>spiritual, of which the literal were types (<reference osisRef="Rom.12.1">Ro 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.13.15">He 13:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.2.5">1Pe 2:5</reference>).<div eID="gen16232" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16233" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">accepted--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Eph.1.6">Ep 1:6</reference>).<div eID="gen16233" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16234" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">altar--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Heb.13.10">He 13:10</reference>), spiritually, the Cross of Christ, which sanctifies our sacrifices of prayer and praise.<div eID="gen16234" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16235" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">house ... for all people--</hi>or rather, "peoples." No longer restricted to one favored people (Mal 1:11; <reference osisRef="John.4.21">Joh 4:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.4.23">23</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Tim.2.8">1Ti 2:8</reference>). To be fully realized at the second coming (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.2-Isa.2.4">Is 2:2-4</reference>). No longer literal, but spiritual sacrifice, namely, "prayer" shall be offered (<reference osisRef="Ps.141.2">Psa 141:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.51.17">51:17</reference>; Mal 1:11; <reference osisRef="Matt.21.13">Mt 21:13</reference>). <div eID="gen16235" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. Even them-- ( Ep 2:11-13 ). to my holy mountain-- Jerusalem, the seat of the Lord's throne in His coming kingdom ( Is 2:2 ; Jr 3:17 ). joyful-- ( Ro 5:11 ). burnt offerings ... sacrifices-- spiritual, of which the literal were types ( Ro 12:1 ; He 13:15 ; 1Pe 2:5 ). accepted-- ( Ep 1:6 ). altar-- ( He 13:10 ), spiritually, the Cross of Christ, which sanctifies our sacrifices of prayer and praise. house ... for all people-- or rather, "peoples." No longer restricted to one favored people (Mal 1:11; Joh 4:21 , 23 ; 1Ti 2:8 ). To be fully realized at the second coming ( Is 2:2-4 ). No longer literal, but spiritual sacrifice, namely, "prayer" shall be offered ( Psa 141:2 ; 51:17 ; Mal 1:11; Mt 21:13 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9388"/><div sID="gen16237" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9388"/><hi type="bold">9. beasts--</hi>Gentile idolatrous nations hostile to the Jews, summoned by God to chastise them (Jr 12:7-9; 50:<reference osisRef="Jer.9.17">17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.34.5">Eze 34:5</reference>): the Chaldeans and subsequently the Romans. entries.reader_content_plain: 11. greedy-- literally, "strong" (that is, insatiable) in appetite ( Eze 34:2 , 3 ; Mi 3:11 ). cannot understand-- unable to comprehend the wants of the people, spiritually: so Is 56:10 , "cannot bark." look to ... own way-- that is, their own selfish interests; not to the spiritual welfare of the people ( Jr 6:13 ; Eze 22:27 ). from his quarter-- rather, "from the highest to the lowest" [Lowth]. "From his quarter"; that is, from one end to the other of them, one and all ( Ge 19:4 ).
